hook: Follow a small office disaster from black screen to rescue, and learn to spot what went wrong, what saved the day and what changed.
intro: A short narrative of about 200 words about a mishap — Herr Klein’s computer dies on the morning of his presentation — told in the Präteritum, with one step further back in the Plusquamperfekt (hatte … geschickt), several passives (wurde geöffnet, wurde abgeholt, repariert werden konnte) and a since-then in the present (Seitdem speichert er …). Blog posts and stories like this are everyday reading, and you read them for what happened, how it was solved and what changed. The six questions follow the narrative: the problem, what customer service said, the rescue, the talk, the next day and the lesson. The technology vocabulary from earlier in the module comes back in context — einschalten, Bildschirm, Festplatte, gespeichert, Gerät, Datei, Kundendienst.
tips[0].title: Problem → solution → lesson
tips[0].text: Find the three parts: what went wrong (der Bildschirm blieb schwarz), how it was fixed (Zum Glück …), what he does now (Seitdem …). Each part carries at least one question.
tips[0].check.why: Zum Glück introduces the rescue: something goes right after the problem.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Problem
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Solution
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Lesson
tips[1].title: Plusquamperfekt = the step before the story
tips[1].text: hatte … geschickt happened the evening before the story’s morning — and it is the key to the rescue. When a narrative in the Präteritum switches to hatte / war + participle, it is looking further back.
tips[1].check.why: war abgefahren is the Plusquamperfekt: it looks one step further back than ankamen.
tips[2].title: The passive hides who did it
tips[2].text: wurde geöffnet, wurde abgeholt: the text does not say by whom, because it does not matter. Questions about these sentences ask what happened, not who did it.
tips[2].check.why: The passive tells you what happened and leaves out who did it.
remember[0]: Past for what happened, hatte + participle for what came before, present after seitdem for what changed.
exam: Short personal narratives like this blog post are a standard reading text in the B1 exam.
tips[0].check.q: „Zum Glück fand der Techniker den Fehler schnell.“ Which part of a story is this?
tips[1].check.q: „Als wir ankamen, war der Zug schon abgefahren.“ What happened first?
tips[2].check.q: „Das Paket wurde gestern geliefert.“ What does this sentence tell you?
